case_title: Nitya Nand v. State of U.P. & Anr.
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (the appellant's father Shree Dev was the victim's brother); prior enmity and property dispute
statutory_provisions: IPC s.148; IPC s.302 read with s.149
weapon: Country-made pistol (fired into the air by the appellant); kanta and knives used on the victim; danda also carried by one accused
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW-1 and PW-2); medical (post-mortem and testimony of PW-3)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.148 IPC (RI two years, fine Rs. 2,000) and s.302/149 IPC (life imprisonment)
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence affirmed
offence_finally_established: Rioting armed with a deadly weapon (IPC s.148) and murder under IPC s.302 read with s.149
neutral_facts: On the afternoon of 8 September 1992, the victim went to a riverside ghat to bathe, accompanied by his son and his brother. Near the ghat, a group of men approached from the direction of a park. According to the eyewitness accounts, the group included the accused, who was carrying a country-made pistol, and other persons armed with a danda, kanta and knives. The group confronted the victim, caught hold of him and assaulted him with kanta and knives. On hearing his cries for help, the victim's son, another witness and the victim's brother ran towards the spot. As they approached, the accused fired a shot into the air from the pistol, after which the group fled from the scene through the south-western side. The victim was found dead on the steps of the ghat with his body partly in the water. A post-mortem examination recorded multiple incised and stab wounds on the head, face, neck, chest, back and arm, and the doctor opined that death was possibly caused by shock and haemorrhage from sharp-edged weapons. A written report was lodged at the police station shortly after the incident, and the investigating officers recorded statements of witnesses. Prior litigation between the families over property formed the background to the incident. No country-made pistol or cartridge was recovered from the scene.
offence_severity: Not stated for s.302 (the judgment does not state its punishment); s.148 IPC: imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both
physical_harm: Death of the victim from multiple incised and stab wounds to the head, face, neck, chest, back and arm
motive: alleged: property dispute and old enmity arising from the victim's brother's will in favour of the victim's sons
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PW-1 and PW-2 on the appellant's presence in the group and his firing into the air; medical evidence of PW-3 establishing homicidal death
witness_credibility: PW-1 and PW-2 found categorical and unshaken in cross-examination; PW-2 said he saw the incident with his own eyes
bail_history: Bail rejected by the Supreme Court on 30.06.2014 (while granting leave); no other bail history stated
trial_duration: offence: 08.09.1992; trial judgment: 20.01.1997; High Court: 27.09.2012; Supreme Court: 04.09.2024
legal_representation: Appellant: P. K. Jain, Saurabh Jain, S.P. Singh Rathore and others (Advocates). Respondents (State of U.P. and another): Goutham Shivhankar, Ms. Ruchira Goel and others (Advocates)
investigation_status: FIR registered (Crime No. 237/1992); investigation completed; chargesheet filed 13.10.1992; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Scribe and Laxmi Narain not examined; no country-made pistol or cartridge recovered; blood sample from the stairs not sent for chemical examination. The court acknowledged these lacunae but did not treat them as fatal
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.148 and s.302/149 IPC; High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence affirmed; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Clear motive from the property dispute; the appellant was part of the unlawful assembly with common object to kill; firing to enable escape was an overt act; non-recovery of the pistol not fatal; ocular evidence supported by medical evidence; the key eyewitness Laxmi Narain was later killed, so could not be examined
defence_argument: No firearm injuries and no recovery of pistol or cartridge; the appellant's role was only firing into the air; the omission to examine Laxmi Narain and the scribe Kuldeep was fatal; conviction based on suspicion, so the benefit of doubt should be given
legal_principle_applied: Section 149 IPC creates vicarious liability; the question is whether the accused was a member of the unlawful assembly, not whether he actually took active part; no overt act need be imputed to the individual member
precedent_relied_upon: Krishnappa v. State of Karnataka [2012] 6 SCR 1068 : (2012) 11 SCC 237; Vinubhai Ranchhodbhai Patel v. Rajivbhai Dudabhai Patel [2018] 6 SCR 1050 : (2018) 7 SCC 743; Yunis alias Kariya v. State of M.P. (2003) 1 SCC 425
